n4-imouto: A <radical>woman</radical> climbs a <radical>tree</radical> to escape her chores. She gets stuck halfway up, laughing instead of coming down. Mom sighs, because that is exactly how your <kanji>younger sister</kanji> behaves.
n4-kariru: Each <radical>day</radical>, a <radical>person</radical> sneaks over and takes <radical>two</radical> cups from next door. He promises to bring them back by evening. Taking something you plan to give back is <kanji>borrowing</kanji>.
n4-karui: A <radical>vehicle</radical> hauls a heavy pile of <radical>earth</radical> down the road. A hand reaches in <radical>again</radical> and scoops dirt off the top. Soon the cart rolls along <kanji>light</kanji> and empty.
n4-kasu: A <radical>person</radical> plants a <radical>stake</radical> to mark a deal. Then hands a <radical>shell</radical> full of coins to a neighbor. That is how you <kanji>lend</kanji> something valuable.
n4-kiru-wear: A <radical>sheep</radical> arrives at the door, coat caught on its horns. A giant <radical>eye</radical> in the peephole spots it and swings the door open. The sheep walks in still <kanji>wearing</kanji> its coat.
n4-kurai: The <radical>sun</radical> is just rising over the shrine steps. A huge cat rears up to <radical>stand</radical> in the doorway, blocking all the light. Its shadow swallows the steps, and everything turns <kanji>dark</kanji>.
n4-modoru: A raccoon rams through the <radical>door</radical> to steal a snack. It runs off, then feels guilty and turns around. Minutes later it walks back through the same door, making a perfect <kanji>return</kanji>.
n4-oboeru: A creature that only wants to <radical>see</radical> creeps toward a huge bell. A thick <radical>cover</radical> drops over it, blocking every bit of light. Blind now, it burns the bell's shape into memory and will always <kanji>remember</kanji> it.
